GLOSSARY.SEARCH_PLACEHOLDER: Search financial term (e.g. fund, inflation, interest, credit, liquidity)...

emergency-fund.SHORT_DESC: Your financial safety net for unexpected life events.
emergency-fund.EXPLANATION: A pool of money set aside exclusively for genuine emergencies (medical bills, urgent car repairs, or temporary job loss). Ideally, it covers 3 to 6 months of basic living costs.
emergency-fund.EXAMPLE: If your basic monthly living costs are Q3,000, a 3-month fund is Q9,000.

micro-expenses.SHORT_DESC: Small, daily purchases that go largely unnoticed.
micro-expenses.EXPLANATION: Inconspicuous everyday purchases (daily coffee on the way to work, snacks, extra delivery tips, unused app subscriptions). Individually minor, but together they drain hundreds or thousands yearly.
micro-expenses.EXAMPLE: Spending Q20 daily on snacks equals Q600 per month and Q7,200 per year.

rule-50-30-20.SHORT_DESC: A straightforward formula for managing monthly income.
rule-50-30-20.EXPLANATION: A classic budgeting blueprint: 50% for Needs (housing, food, utilities), 30% for Wants (lifestyle, entertainment), and 20% for Savings and debt repayment.
rule-50-30-20.EXAMPLE: On a Q5,000 salary: Q2,500 for essentials, Q1,500 for lifestyle, and Q1,000 for savings.

compound-interest.SHORT_DESC: Earning interest on interest you have already accumulated.
compound-interest.EXPLANATION: The exponential growth of money over time. When you save or invest, your yields are added to your principal, meaning future returns are calculated on a progressively larger base.
compound-interest.EXAMPLE: Saving Q1,000 at 5% annually earns Q50 in year one. In year two, you earn 5% on Q1,050.

full-payer.SHORT_DESC: Someone who pays 100% of their credit card balance every month.
full-payer.EXPLANATION: Paying the entire statement balance before the due date, enjoying all card perks (security, points, cashflow cushion) without paying any interest or financing charges.
full-payer.EXAMPLE: If you spend Q800 during the billing cycle, you pay back exactly Q800 on the due date.

inflation.SHORT_DESC: The general increase in prices and gradual loss of purchasing power.
inflation.EXPLANATION: When everyday goods and services grow more expensive over time, meaning the same amount of cash buys less than before. Cash left idle loses value.
inflation.EXAMPLE: If a lunch cost Q30 last year and Q33 today, the annual inflation rate was 10%.

liquidity.SHORT_DESC: How quickly and easily an asset can be converted into spendable cash.
liquidity.EXPLANATION: Money in your CURBI bank account is 100% liquid because you can transfer it instantly. Real estate or vehicles have low liquidity because selling them takes weeks or months.
liquidity.EXAMPLE: Money in your checking or savings account provides instant liquidity.

zero-based-budget.SHORT_DESC: Giving every single incoming cent a defined purpose.
zero-based-budget.EXPLANATION: Allocating every quetzal of your income to a category (needs, desires, savings, debt) until Income minus Outflows equals zero. It means total intention, not reckless spending.
zero-based-budget.EXAMPLE: If you earn Q4,000, you allocate all Q4,000 across your categories and goals.
